about: Route is a Lehi, Utah e-commerce software company whose app provides package tracking, shipping protection insurance and delivery updates for online shoppers and merchants on platforms such as Shopify. Founded in 2018, it was valued at 2 billion dollars in 2021 and has raised about $289 million. Merchants pay for shipping protection offered at checkout, while consumers use the free app. It is a consumer-facing app and B2B platform, with moderate awareness among online shoppers.

TickPick is a New York based online ticket marketplace for sports, concerts and theatre that sells tickets without buyer fees, showing all-in prices, and lets users bid on tickets. Founded in 2011 by Brett Goldberg and Lance Hauser, it makes money from seller fees. It has sold tens of millions of tickets, and runs advertising and sponsorship in sports. Funding shown is about $290 million. It is a consumer brand with national awareness among US ticket buyers.

Wallapop is a Barcelona based Spanish second-hand marketplace app where users buy and sell used goods such as phones, clothes, furniture and cars locally, with shipping and payment options. Founded in 2013, it has tens of millions of downloads and is among the most used classified apps in Spain, and it merged its Spanish operations with Milanuncios in 2023. Funding shown is about 260 million euros. It is a prominent consumer brand in Spain, with large advertising campaigns.

FreshToHome is a Bengaluru based Indian online platform selling fresh fish, meat, seafood and chemical-free groceries, delivered to customers in major cities and the UAE. It processes products in its own facilities, with a supply chain linked to fishermen and farms. Founded in 2015 by Shan Kadavil, it has raised about $256 million, including funding from Amazon and others. It sells directly to consumers via its app and is a widely advertised food delivery brand in India.

Slope is a San Francisco B2B payments and financial platform offering net terms, invoicing and credit for business-to-business purchases, particularly for suppliers who want to give buyers payment flexibility. It handles credit underwriting, collections and payment collection. Founded in 2020, it has raised about $252 million including debt financing. It is a B2B fintech serving businesses in sectors such as industrial and e-commerce suppliers, with little consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Slope is a B2B financial platform that offers a variety o...

about: RatePAY is a Berlin based German payment service provider offering online shops buy-now-pay-later options such as invoice and instalment payment, including credit checks and payment risk handling. Founded in 2009, it serves merchants in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands, and shoppers see it as a payment option at checkout. Crunchbase shows funding of around 208 million. Its ownership is not stated in the input. It is a B2B payments brand with limited consumer awareness.
cb_desc: RatePAY offers secure payment solutions for online trading.

about: Raise is a Chicago based online marketplace for buying and selling discounted gift cards, where consumers sell unwanted cards and others buy them below face value, plus a rewards programme. Founded in 2013, it has raised about $210 million from investors including Accel and Foundation Capital. Revenue comes from the spread on card sales and partner commissions. It is a consumer brand with moderate awareness among US deal shoppers.

about: Magalu (Magazine Luiza) is a Sao Paulo based Brazilian retailer and e-commerce platform selling electronics, appliances, furniture and a wide range of products through hundreds of stores and an online marketplace, with a virtual assistant named Lu. Founded in 1957 in Franca, it is among Brazil's largest retailers and is listed on B3 (MGLU3). Customers are mass-market Brazilian consumers. It is a top-tier consumer brand in Brazil with heavy advertising and sponsorship activity.

Thinkific is a Vancouver based software platform that lets entrepreneurs, creators and businesses build, market and sell online courses, memberships and communities. It earns subscription fees from paying course creators, and has helped sell many millions of courses. Founded in 2012, it listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (THNC) in 2021 and has raised about $193 million. It is a B2B and creator economy brand with niche awareness among online educators.

Boqii is a Shanghai based Chinese pet-focused online platform, listed on the NYSE (BQ), which sells pet food, supplies and healthcare products through its e-commerce site and offline stores, and runs a pet community and content platform. Founded in 2010, it targets pet owners in China's fast-growing pet market. It has raised about $151 million before its 2020 IPO. It is a recognizable pet consumer brand in China.

Spryker is a Berlin based commerce technology company offering a modular platform for B2B and B2C e-commerce, marketplaces and enterprise portals, which companies use to build their online selling. Customers include industrial firms, retailers and consumer brands around the world. Founded in 2014, it has raised about $152 million from investors including TCV and Project A. It is a B2B software brand, little known to consumers.

BLK Global is a UK company based in Glasgow, Scotland, which Crunchbase lists under consulting and e-commerce. The input flags it as listed and shows funding of about 64 million dollars, but gives no description. Its products, customers and scale are not supported by the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LightInTheBox is a Chinese online retailer, originally based in Beijing, selling apparel, home goods, small accessories and party dresses to consumers worldwide, with major markets in Europe and North America. Listed on the NYSE (LITB) since 2013. Cross-border e-commerce brand with moderate awareness among online shoppers.

Wheels India is an Indian maker of steel wheels for commercial vehicles, tractors, passenger cars and construction equipment, based in Chennai and part of the TVS group. It supplies automakers such as Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland and Mahindra and also exports. Listed on the NSE and BSE. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

EShallGo is a Chinese company based in Shanghai, listed on Nasdaq (EHGO), in e-commerce and leasing, operating a platform for IT hardware leasing and recycling aimed at small businesses, and for second-hand electronics. It has raised about 28 million dollars. B2B service with limited public brand awareness.

Society Pass is a Southeast Asian loyalty and e-commerce ecosystem company, with its head office in Singapore and operations in Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand, running consumer loyalty, ride-hailing, food delivery and advertising businesses. Listed on Nasdaq (SOPA) since 2021. Consumer-facing brands with regional presence and limited global awareness.

Wunong Net Technology is a Chinese online food retailer, based in Shenzhen, selling agricultural products and fresh food to consumers and businesses through its e-commerce platform and has been listed on Nasdaq (WNW) since 2020. It is a small business with funding of about 30 million dollars and limited brand awareness outside its local market.

Akelius is a Swedish residential property company, based in Stockholm, that owns and renovates apartments for rent in Sweden, Germany, the UK, France, Denmark, Canada and the US, with a portfolio of tens of thousands of flats. Founded by Roger Akelius, it is privately held and funds itself through bonds. Customers are tenants. Notable as a landlord rather than a consumer brand.

Condis Supermercats is a Catalan supermarket chain, based in Begues near Barcelona, with about 600 stores in Catalonia and neighbouring regions, mostly franchised, and an online delivery service. It is privately held. Customers are local households. Strong regional consumer brand in Catalonia.

EET Retail is the fuel retail arm of Essar Energy Transition, the owner of the Stanlow refinery in Cheshire, selling petrol and diesel through forecourts and commercial fuels in the UK. Based at Stanlow, Shropshire. Part of the Essar group of India. Customers are motorists and fleets. Mid-profile fuel brand.

about: ContextLogic is the company behind Wish, the mobile shopping marketplace that sold low-priced goods, often shipped from China, directly to consumers. It listed on Nasdaq in 2020 (WISH), but sales collapsed, and in 2024 it sold the Wish platform to Qoo10 (Singapore) for 173 million dollars and became a shell company with cash and tax assets. Headquartered in Oakland, California, previously San Francisco, founded 2010 by Peter Szulczewski and Danny Zhang. Funding of about 1.6 billion dollars. Wish was a well-known mobile shopping app but is no longer an operating company.

Steinhoff Africa Retail was the retail arm of the Steinhoff group, listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in 2017 and renamed Pepkor Holdings (JSE: PPH) in 2018. Its brands include Pep and Ackermans (value clothing and homeware), PEP Home, JD Group furniture banners such as Russells and Bradlows, and Tiger Wheel & Tyre. It serves value-oriented shoppers across South Africa and neighbouring countries through thousands of stores. Strong brand awareness in Southern Africa, particularly among lower-income households.
cb_desc: Steinhoff's emerging and developed market retail

about: TMON (Ticket Monster) is a South Korean e-commerce platform that began as a daily-deal site and sells tickets, travel, local services and general merchandise to consumers through its app and website. Headquartered in Seoul, it was previously owned by LivingSocial and Groupon, and later by KKR and Anchor Equity Partners. In 2022 it was acquired by Qoo10 owner Qoo Group (Singapore), and in 2024 it was caught up in the TMON and WeMakePrice settlement-delay crisis and entered court receivership. Known Korean consumer brand with troubled finances.

about: Babytree is a Chinese parenting and maternal community platform that began as a forum in 2007 and grew into an app with content, social features and e-commerce for expectant and new parents. It earns revenue from advertising, online sales of baby products and health services. Headquartered in Beijing, it has tens of millions of monthly active users, and was backed by Tencent and other investors, with about 1 billion dollars of funding shown. It went public in Hong Kong (1761) and later its e-commerce Meitun business was a major part. Well-known mother-and-baby consumer brand in China.

Bitauto Holdings is a Chinese automotive internet services company running Yiche, an online platform for new and used car information, advertising and transaction services. It earns revenue from advertising by automakers and dealers and from a transaction services platform. Headquartered in Beijing, it was listed on the NYSE (BITA) from 2010, backed by Tencent, JD.com and Baidu, and in 2020 was taken private by a consortium that included Tencent and Hillhouse. Well-known auto portal in China, B2B2C in nature, with buying-intent audience.

Qunar.com is a major Chinese online travel platform and search engine for flights, hotels and tour packages, headquartered in Beijing and founded in 2005. Baidu owned a majority stake, and Qunar listed on Nasdaq in 2013 (QUNR) before merging with Ctrip (Trip.com Group) in 2015, with Ctrip taking a stake and Baidu receiving shares. After the Ctrip tie-up it was taken private. Customers are consumers and travel suppliers. Well-known Chinese travel brand with an active mobile app user base.

Red Star Macalline is a leading Chinese home furnishing mall operator, with over 300 large shopping malls and branded stores across China where furniture makers, brands and retailers lease space. Headquartered in Shanghai, founded in 1986 by Che Jianxin family and listed in Hong Kong (1528) and Shanghai (601828). It has expanded into e-commerce, home design and platform services. In 2023-24 it was acquired in part by Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall interests; control shifted to Yinhai Zhongnan. Recognized consumer brand across Chinese cities, with housing-market exposure.

Carzone (Chezhi) is a Shanghai-based Chinese auto parts e-commerce platform, which sells car components, accessories and maintenance services to car owners and workshops online. Its funding of around 700 million dollars suggests large venture financing. The available information does not confirm which listing, if any, the company has or how many customers it serves. Operates in the automotive aftermarket in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Carzone is an e-commerce platform for auto parts.

about: ManoMano is a French online marketplace for DIY, home improvement and gardening products, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Paris. It lists several million products from merchants and sells to consumers and professionals in France, Spain, Italy, Germany, the UK and Belgium. Backed by Eurazeo, Bain Capital Ventures, General Atlantic and Aglae, it was valued at roughly 2.6 billion euros in 2021. Revenue came from commissions and advertising. Strong consumer brand awareness in France and Southern Europe, with TV advertising.

StockX is a Detroit-based online marketplace for sneakers, streetwear, electronics, collectibles and trading cards, which works like a stock market with live bids and asks and authenticates items in its own centres. It earns a transaction fee and seller fee on each sale and serves millions of buyers and sellers worldwide. Founded in 2015 by Dan Gilbert, Josh Luber and others, it was valued at about 3.8 billion dollars in 2021. It has had legal disputes with Nike. Strong brand with younger sneaker-focused consumers.

Tuhu (Tuhu Car Care, 途虎养车) is a Chinese car maintenance and parts platform operating online-to-offline: customers order tyres, oil, batteries and servicing online and have them fitted at a network of thousands of partner workshops and company-run stores. Headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2011, it listed in Hong Kong in 2025 (9690). It is backed by Tencent, Sequoia China and other investors, and is a significant name in Chinese automotive aftermarket services. Recognized consumer auto service brand in China.

Christian Louboutin is the French luxury fashion house of designer Christian Louboutin, founded in 1991 and famous for women's shoes with red lacquered soles, and now also men's shoes, handbags, beauty and eyewear. It sells through its own boutiques and e-commerce store and selected department stores worldwide. Based in Paris, it is privately held, with Exor (Agnelli family) buying a minority stake in 2021. Revenue is estimated at several hundred million euros. Very strong luxury consumer brand recognition.

Kajabi is an all-in-one platform for knowledge entrepreneurs and creators to build, market and sell online courses, memberships, coaching and podcasts, bundling website, email, payments and community tools. Based in Irvine, California, and founded in 2010 by Kenny Rueter and Travis Rosser, it earns monthly subscriptions from tens of thousands of creator businesses. It raised 550 million dollars from Tiger Global and Insight Partners and others. Well known among online creators, little general consumer awareness.

Movile is a Brazilian technology and investment group, parent of iFood, the leading Brazilian food delivery app, and the owner of other apps and holdings such as Sympla (events), Rappi stake interests and Zoop. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, it is backed by Naspers/Prosus and Innova Capital. Its main value lies in iFood, which has tens of millions of orders per month. Movile itself is a holding with lower public visibility, while iFood is a household name in Brazil.

about: Trader Interactive is a US digital marketplace operator for commercial and recreational vehicle classifieds. Its sites include RV Trader, Cycle Trader, Commercial Truck Trader, Equipment Trader, Boat Trader-like listings and Dealer Spike tools. It earns subscription and advertising fees from dealers and sellers, and offers software for dealer management. Headquartered in Virginia Beach, Virginia, it was formed from Dominion Enterprises assets and owned by Apax Partners since 2021 after Insight Partners-owned stewardship. B2B2C classifieds, known among RV and motorcycle buyers.

about: Moglix is a Singapore- and India-based B2B e-commerce and supply chain platform for industrial products and business supplies, founded in 2015 by Rahul Garg, selling tools, safety equipment, electricals and raw materials to manufacturers and contractors, and also providing financing and sourcing services. It has raised around 470 million dollars from Tiger Global, Accel, Jungle Ventures and others, with operations in India and the Gulf. B2B marketplace with little consumer awareness.

Ruigu (Ruigu, 睿谷) is a Shanghai-based Chinese B2B e-commerce platform focused on the sale of electronics and hardware components, with funding of around 500 million dollars shown. The input does not state the owners, customers or turnover. It likely supplies industrial or electronic components to business buyers across China. B2B with no consumer visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Shift Technologies was a San Francisco online marketplace for used cars, founded in 2013, which bought cars from consumers, reconditioned them and sold them online with home delivery in several US states. It listed on Nasdaq in 2020 through a SPAC with Insurance Acquisition Corp (SFT), then merged with CarLotz in 2022. It could not sustain losses and filed for Chapter 11 in October 2023, with operations wound down. Funding around 504 million dollars. No longer operating.

Ankorstore is a Paris-based European wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with brands, letting shops order from many brands with free shipping and flexible payment terms. Founded in 2019 by Jean-Baptiste Hironde, Nicolas Rebut and others, it serves tens of thousands of brands and over 100,000 retailers across Europe. It was valued at 1.7 billion euros in 2022, with backers including Bain Capital Ventures, Tiger Global and Index Ventures. B2B marketplace, widely known to boutique shop owners.

Balance is a New York fintech offering a B2B payments platform that gives businesses buy-now-pay-later and net-terms checkout and invoicing, so sellers get paid upfront while buyers pay later. Founded in 2021 by Ofir Blank, Anna Elvik and Yonatan Fisher, it has raised funds from Viola, Valar Ventures and Hyperion-like investors. Funding shown is about 437 million dollars including debt. B2B payments brand, known among e-commerce and marketplace operators.

about: ElasticRun is a Pune-based Indian logistics and distribution platform that connects manufacturers with rural kirana (small grocery) stores through a network of independent gig-style delivery partners, supplying fast-moving consumer goods. Founded in 2015 by Sandeep Deshmukh and Shitiz Bansal, it raised around 430 million dollars from Prosus, Avataar, Goldman Sachs and Kalaari Capital. It also operates the Grow platform for retailers. B2B brand known among rural retailers and large FMCG companies.

Modalku (now Funding Societies | Modalku) is a Southeast Asian digital financing platform headquartered in Singapore, with an Indonesian arm in Jakarta, that connects small businesses with lenders and provides loans, invoice financing and a business banking app. Founded in 2015, it has funded billions of dollars of loans across Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, backed by SoftBank Ventures Asia, Sequoia India and Visa. B2B fintech with reasonable recognition among SMEs in the region.

Rent-A-Center (now Upbound Group) is a US rent-to-own retailer that leases furniture, appliances, electronics and computers to consumers on weekly or monthly payment plans, mostly to customers with limited credit access. It operates about 1,800 stores under the Rent-A-Center and Acima brands and a Brigit financial app, with revenue near 4 billion dollars. Based in Plano, Texas, and listed on Nasdaq (UPBD after 2023 rebrand). Recognized US consumer retailer brand.

CassTime is a Shenzhen-based auto parts e-commerce platform in China serving car owners and workshops, selling components and maintenance supplies online. The input shows funding of about 350 million dollars. It likely competes with other automotive aftermarket platforms such as Tuhu. Further details on ownership and scale are not given in the input. Consumer and workshop-facing brand in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Frubana is a Bogota-based B2B food supply platform for restaurants in Latin America, delivering fresh produce and ingredients sourced from farmers and suppliers to restaurants in Colombia, Brazil and Mexico. Founded in 2018, it is a one-stop shop for restaurant owners combining e-commerce and logistics. Funding of about 351 million dollars is shown, including debt. B2B with little consumer awareness.

about: Mensa Brands is a Bengaluru-based Indian internet-first company that acquires and scales direct-to-consumer brands, mostly in fashion, beauty and home, selling through Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and its own sites. Founded in 2021 by Ananth Narayanan (formerly of Myntra and Mensa), it raised money at around 1 billion dollars valuation from Accel, Falcon Edge and Norwest. It has since cut staff and restructured. B2C brand portfolio; the parent has low awareness.

Caixa Economica Federal is Brazil's state-owned federal savings bank, founded in 1861 and headquartered in Brasilia, with tens of thousands of branches and lottery outlets, and a vast retail customer base of over 150 million accounts. It runs mortgage lending, FGTS worker funds, Bolsa Familia payments, government social programmes and the national lotteries. Wholly owned by the Brazilian government. Huge consumer brand in Brazil, with major sports sponsorships in football, the Olympic movement and others.

Flip is a Los Angeles-based social commerce platform and shopping app in which creators and shoppers share videos about products, including beauty, fashion and home goods, and can buy inside the app. Funding of about 239 million dollars is shown. Customers are younger online shoppers. Mid-profile consumer app. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Chrono24 is the world's largest online marketplace for luxury watches, connecting private sellers and professional dealers with buyers in more than 100 countries, with several hundred thousand listings including Rolex, Patek Philippe and Audemars Piguet. It earns commissions and listing fees, and offers an escrow-style payment service. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, it employs around 700 people and took a major investment from General Atlantic in 2021. Well-known consumer brand among watch enthusiasts and an obvious fit with premium luxury sponsorship.

Fairplay is a Mexico City fintech offering performance-based financing to e-commerce and digital businesses, lending against sales and marketing performance so sellers can fund inventory and advertising. Customers are online merchants and consumer brands in Latin America, and revenue comes from fees and interest. It has raised around $200 million in a combination of equity and debt funding. B2B finance with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: RWB is the merged business of Wildberries and Russ, the operator of Russia's largest e-commerce marketplace, Wildberries, which sells fashion, electronics, home goods and more online through a vast network of pickup points and warehouses, also covering logistics and payments. The merger was announced in 2024 and closed in 2025, combining Wildberries with Russ (which runs businesses including the Russ Outdoor advertising firm). Founded by Tatyana Bakalchuk and based in Moscow, serving tens of millions of customers in Russia and neighbouring markets. Very high consumer visibility in Russia and CIS. Sanctions and Russian-market considerations apply for sponsorship.

about: Farcaster is a decentralised social network protocol and app ecosystem, with the main client Warpcast, that lets users own their identities and posts via Ethereum, popular with crypto developers and creators. Its parent company, Merkle Manufactory (San Francisco/Los Angeles), raised $150 million in a 2024 round led by Paradigm, taking total funding to about $180 million. Revenue is limited, from storage rent and token-related products. In 2025 the Farcaster team was acquired by Neynar. Niche consumer crypto brand.

Parker is a New York fintech offering corporate credit cards and spend management designed for e-commerce brands, with credit limits based on revenue and cash flow instead of personal guarantees. Founded in 2020 by Yaniv Mehr, it raised around $177 million in funding including debt facilities, but it shut down its operations in 2024-25 following a financial collapse. Customers were online merchants. Little consumer brand awareness.

about: Moladin is a Jakarta-based automotive financing and e-commerce platform in Indonesia offering vehicle financing, used-car and motorcycle sales through its app and partners, as well as dealer services. Founded in 2020, it has raised about $173 million in equity and debt, including funding from Alpha JWC and others. Customers are Indonesian car and motorcycle buyers and dealers, with revenue from financing and fees. Moderate regional brand awareness.

about: SIRCLO is an Indonesian e-commerce enabler, based in Tangerang near Jakarta, offering a website-building platform (SIRCLO Store), omnichannel selling tools and fulfilment services that let brands and sellers run online shops and marketplace operations. Customers are Indonesian small businesses and consumer brands. Founded in 2009 as Mediatrack, it has raised about $171 million, including from Bain Capital, and has grown into a large e-commerce services group. B2B with modest brand awareness.

about: Ula is an Indonesian B2B e-commerce marketplace, based in Jakarta, that lets small neighbourhood retailers (warungs) order groceries and daily goods in bulk with credit and delivery through its app. Founded in 2020, it has raised about $168 million, including a $87 million Series B in 2021 led by Tiger Global and Lightspeed. Revenue comes from product margins and fees. B2B brand known mainly to small shopkeepers in Indonesia.

AvenuesAI is an Indian company based in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, which Crunchbase classes under e-commerce and financial services; the row came from a search of listed companies, with funding shown as 7.4 billion rupees. No description was captured and the specific products, customers and scale are not clear from the input. It appears to be a payments or digital commerce technology business with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Carma is an Australian online used-car marketplace and retailer based in Redfern, Sydney, where buyers can browse, finance and have cars delivered, and sellers can sell their cars online. The row came from a search for listed companies, and Crunchbase shows funding of about A$133 million. Revenue is from vehicle sales and finance and service fees. Details of the listing and scale were not confirmed. Consumer-facing brand with moderate awareness in Australia. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Holaluz is a Barcelona-based Spanish electricity and solar company that sells renewable-sourced power and rooftop solar installation to households and businesses, along with a community-sharing platform for solar surplus, and has a few hundred thousand customers. Founded in 2010, it is listed on BME Growth in Madrid and was an early B Corp. Revenue is from electricity retail and solar. Moderate consumer brand awareness in Spain.

Fanhua Inc. is a Guangzhou-based Chinese financial services and insurance intermediary, formerly called CNinsure, distributing life and property insurance products through agents and its digital platforms. It was listed on Nasdaq under FANH. Customers are Chinese individuals and businesses buying insurance, and revenue comes from commissions. Funding of about $32 million is shown. Moderate brand profile in China, with little international consumer awareness.

Alok Industries is an Indian vertically integrated textile company, based in Thane, Maharashtra, making cotton and polyester yarn, apparel and home textiles such as fabrics, towels and bedding, sold in India and overseas. After insolvency proceedings, it was taken over in 2019 by a consortium led by Reliance Industries and JM Financial Asset Reconstruction. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Mostly B2B and retail-channel textiles with moderate consumer awareness.

Tokmanni Group is a Finnish discount variety retailer, operating Tokmanni and Dollarstore in Finland, Sweden and Denmark, selling household goods, food, textiles, cosmetics, toys and seasonal items at low prices through several hundred stores. Based in Mantsala, Finland, it is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki and had revenue of about 1.7 billion euros. Customers are consumers. Strong consumer brand in Finland, with some Nordic-wide visibility.

Kohl's is a US department store chain, based in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, operating around 1,100 stores and a website, selling apparel, shoes, home goods and beauty products from national and private brands such as Sonoma and Apt. 9, with Sephora shops inside stores. Listed on the NYSE under KSS, with revenue near $16 billion. Customers are mid-market US families. Very high consumer brand awareness in the US.

Wittchen is a Polish fashion accessories maker and retailer with headquarters near Warsaw, selling premium leather bags, suitcases, wallets and shoes under the Wittchen brand through about 200 stores, with an online store across Poland, Central Europe and the Baltics. It is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. A recognised consumer brand in Poland, relatively limited elsewhere. It sells through its own stores and website, and is positioned as an affordable premium brand. Its scale is regional, but it is a recognised name for travel goods and leather accessories in Poland.

Yandex.Market is an e-commerce marketplace in Russia owned by Yandex and then split into the Yandex group after its 2024 restructuring, selling electronics, household goods and more through a delivery network. It serves consumers across Russia. The input shows large funding in roubles. A major consumer brand in Russia, a restricted sponsorship territory because of sanctions. Revenue comes from commissions and advertising paid by sellers. It is one of the largest online marketplaces in Russia, but sanctions complicate any international brand association.

BinDawood Holding is a Saudi retail group based in Jeddah that operates the BinDawood and Danube hypermarkets and supermarkets, mainly in Makkah, Jeddah, Riyadh and other Saudi cities, as well as online grocery delivery. It sells groceries, fresh food and household goods to consumers, with dozens of stores and many thousands of employees. Listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) since 2020 after an IPO. The family founded the first store in the 1980s. Well known consumer retail brand in Saudi Arabia.

Refurbed is a Vienna, Austria online marketplace, founded in 2017, selling professionally refurbished electronics such as smartphones, laptops, tablets, headphones and appliances from vetted sellers, with a warranty and a return policy. Customers are European consumers who want cheaper, lower-impact devices, and it earns commissions on sales. It operates in about 10 European markets, has raised about $191 million, and has sold millions of devices. Growing consumer brand in Austria, Germany and other European countries, advertised heavily.

Kobo360 is a Lagos, Nigeria-based logistics technology platform, founded in 2017, often described as an Uber-style marketplace for trucks, connecting shippers with truck owners and drivers across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Togo and Uganda. It provides dispatch, tracking and payments, and earns commissions on freight. It has raised about $164 million from investors including Goldman Sachs and Y Combinator. Known mainly to African shippers and fleet owners, with limited consumer awareness.

LivingSocial was a Washington, D.C. online daily deals marketplace, founded in 2007, that offered discounts on local restaurants, activities and travel, competing with Groupon, and was backed by Amazon, which invested about $175 million. It grew rapidly to dozens of countries, but then shrank as the daily deals model declined. It was acquired by Groupon in 2016. Once a recognisable consumer brand in the US and abroad, it is now defunct as a standalone business.

about: The Exchange, formally the Army and Air Force Exchange Service (AAFES), is a Dallas, Texas-based US Department of Defense retail organisation, with a history over 125 years, that runs stores, restaurants, gas stations, e-commerce and services for active-duty military personnel, retirees and their families on bases worldwide. It sells everyday goods tax-free, and its profits support morale, welfare and recreation programmes. It has more than 20,000 employees and revenue of about $7-8 billion. Strong brand within the US military community.

about: Fang Holdings (formerly SouFun) is a Beijing-based Chinese real estate internet portal, listed in the US as ADS, providing property listings, new home sales, rental, home furnishing and online financing services in China. It earns revenue from listing fees, advertising and commissions, and was once one of the largest property websites in China. It has raised about $706 million in total and has shrunk in recent years. Known as a property site in China, with little recognition outside.

about: Ganji.com was a Beijing-based Chinese classifieds website, founded in 2005, where users listed jobs, housing, used goods, cars and services, competing with 58.com. It raised about $710 million, and merged with 58.com in 2015, forming the 58 Group. The Ganji brand then operated as part of 58.com. At its peak, a major consumer classifieds brand in China.

Le.com (LeTV, Letv) was a Beijing-based Chinese online video and entertainment company, the flagship of the LeEco group founded by Jia Yueting, that offered streaming video, smart TVs, phones and e-commerce. It was listed in Shenzhen as Leshi Internet Information and Technology, and faced a major financial crisis from 2016, with LeEco's collapse. Funding of about 6 billion yuan is shown.
